justifications.c1: Independent HSE and trade-press fines of £80,000 (gate manufacturer, search-confirmed), £30,000 (Samson), £20,000 (West Midlands; F&E Joinery) and £10,000, plus law-firm claim settlements of five figures to £60k+; but most fines are for absent, unsafe or never-adequate LEV and ignored notices, not for capture lost unnoticed between tests.
justifications.c2: The statutory TExT interval is at most 14 months (hseblog and HSE G406, search-confirmed), but the weekly routine check comes only from a secondary council document, and no data shows how often LEV degrades between tests (recorded not found).
justifications.c3: Paid TExT contractors (Nederman, SGS, Element, EM Solutions), LEV logbooks and public framework contracts are documented with a 14-month frequency, but no £ cost per test was found, and the sensor would not replace the statutory TExT.
justifications.c4: COSHH reg 9 requires maintenance and TExT at least every 14 months with records kept five years (search-confirmed), with enforcement in this niche: repeated improvement and prohibition notices and prosecutions for welding-fume control (HSE gate manufacturer release, search-confirmed) and targeted HSE fabrication campaigns.
justifications.c5: Liability sits with the employer and sometimes the managing director, but no H&S manager or works manager advert or budget evidence was found (not searched).
justifications.c6: LEV testing contractors visit every 14 months or sooner (Nederman, SGS, Normec), and Munich Re's HSB, an engineering insurer with UKAS-accredited LEV inspection, offers LEV appraisals (search-confirmed); Nederman also sells connected monitoring, though only for its own units.
justifications.c7: Willingness to pay is shown by OEM platforms (Nederman Insight, KEMPER-Connect, both unpriced) and lab airflow monitors at $1,355–$3,820; the gap (no vendor-neutral cloud retrofit for mixed-brand SME LEV) is argued from OEM lock-in and absence, with no complaints or customer counts.
justifications.c8: Off-the-shelf LoRaWAN differential-pressure nodes exist (Dragino PS-LS-D €152; Adeunis Delta-P with current transformer), but finished devices cost ~€150 and a sub-£50 BOM is not evidenced; fouling of pressure tappings by dust and fume is unaddressed.
justifications.c9: A statutory 14-month test with records kept five years and a recommended logbook give a structural reason for ongoing records, but no comparable subscription price was found.
justifications.c10: Regulator enforcement (HSE press releases, Jersey HSI), trade and regional press (The Star, Citation, Designing Buildings) and claimant material (Irwin Mitchell, occupationalasthma.com forum); the first-hand items concern asthma compensation rather than LEV failing between tests.

weakest: No evidence shows LEV capture actually degrading between tests or what that costs; the fines found punish missing or never-adequate extraction, which a monitor on an existing system does not address.
